name: QATAR

flag.title: Flag of Qatar
flag.note: Maroon with white serrated border (9 points)

lead: Qatar is a small peninsula in the warm Persian Gulf. It is so flat that its highest point is only 103 m. Giant gas fields make it one of the world's richest countries.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Qatar is a thumb-shaped peninsula, almost entirely flat. The coast runs over 600 km. In the south, giant sand dunes tumble into the Gulf at Khor Al Adaid.
Under Qatar's rocky ground lies the North Field, the world's largest gas field not tied to oil. Doha's West Bay skyline barely existed 30 years ago.
animals: The Arabian oryx is Qatar's national animal. By 1972, none were left in the wild. Careful breeding brought it back. Seen side-on, its spear-like horns may have inspired the unicorn legend.
Qatar has the world's second-largest dugong population. Dugongs are gentle sea cows that graze on sea-grass. A falcon hospital in Souq Waqif treats injured birds for free.
culture: A Qatari host first offers guests Arabic coffee. It is bitter and smells of cardamom. Tiny cups have no handles. Wiggle the cup when you have had enough.
Falconry and camel racing fill the sports year. Races run from September to March. Robot jockeys ride the camels.
history: Pearl diving once fed Qatar. Divers held stones between their toes and plunged without tanks. In the 1930s, Japanese cultured pearls flooded the market. The industry collapsed.
Oil was found in 1939 and sold abroad from 1949. Qatar became independent from Britain in 1971. In 1996, its first cargo of liquid gas sailed to Japan. Gas now pays for new stadiums and a metro.
wows: Qatar's North Field holds about 900 trillion cubic feet of gas.
Qatar's 2024 GDP was about US$76,000 per person, top five worldwide.
The 2022 World Cup had all 8 stadiums within 55 km.
Camel races use robot jockeys, with owners driving alongside.
Herds of 600+ dugongs graze in Qatar's Gulf waters.
The Museum of Islamic Art sits on its own artificial island.
Qatar's new metro took seven years and opened in 2019.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: Humps store fat, not water. A thirsty camel can drink 100 litres in minutes.
A pearl grows inside an oyster. Grit gets in, and the oyster coats it in shiny layers.
